Check keys and duplicate rows

Source: R/keys.R
keys.Rd

Stata-style checks of identifying variables and duplicated rows.

  • isid(): Check that the selected columns uniquely identify the rows, like Stata's isid. It confirms a valid key with a message and returns the data invisibly, so it can sit inside a pipeline. Invalid keys raise an error.

  • duplicates_report(): Count how many rows share the same values, like duplicates report.

  • duplicates_tag(): Add the number of other rows with the same values, like duplicates tag, generate().

  • duplicates_list(): Return the duplicated rows, like duplicates list.

  • duplicates_drop(): Keep the first row of each duplicated set, like duplicates drop.

Usage

isid(.data, ..., .missing = FALSE)

duplicates_report(.data, ...)

duplicates_tag(.data, ..., .name = "dup")

duplicates_list(.data, ...)

duplicates_drop(.data, ..., .force = FALSE)

Arguments

.data

A data frame, tibble, or data.table.

...

<tidy-select> The identifying columns. Omit to use all columns. Stata's isid requires an explicit variable list.

.missing

If FALSE (default), isid() errors when an identifying column contains missing values or empty strings, as Stata's isid does without missok. If TRUE, permit these values but still require unique key combinations. Rows are not dropped.

.name

Name of the new column created by duplicates_tag().

.force

If TRUE, allow duplicates_drop() to remove rows that match on the selected columns but differ elsewhere, like Stata's duplicates drop varlist, force. Defaults to FALSE; exact duplicate rows can be dropped without this option.

Value

  • isid(): .data, unchanged and invisibly, after a confirmation message.

  • duplicates_report(): a tibble with one row per number of copies: copies, observations (rows with that many copies) and surplus (rows beyond the first of each set).

  • duplicates_tag(): .data with an integer column of the number of other rows sharing the same values (0 for unique rows).

  • duplicates_list(): the duplicated rows, ordered by their identifying values, with .dup_group (set number) and .row (original position).

  • duplicates_drop(): .data without surplus rows, keeping the first row of each set in input order.

The input's data.frame, tibble, data.table or grouped container is kept where rows or columns of .data are returned.

Details

Unlike Stata's silent success, isid() names the columns that form a valid key. This confirms uniqueness without storing an ID declaration or adding metadata. Use suppressMessages() for silent execution. An empty input reports that there are no rows to check. Checks preserve row order. Instead of Stata's sort and using options, use dplyr::arrange() to sort or haven::read_dta() to read a file first. Factor values equal to "" are empty strings; whitespace is not trimmed.

Duplicate identity follows stored values: ordinary and tagged NA values count as equal, NaN is a separate value, and distinct stored SPSS user-missing codes remain distinct. This differs from isid()'s default validation, which rejects all of these missing values; .missing = TRUE permits them while still checking uniqueness by stored-value identity. Checks and duplicate counts use the whole input, regardless of grouping. duplicates_list() rejects existing .dup_group or .row columns; rename them first. duplicates_drop() reports the number of rows removed as a message. The input data are not modified.

See also

Other data checking functions: assert(), is_first(), stata_merge()

Examples

panel <- tibble::tibble(
  id = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3),
  wave = c(1, 2, 1, 1, 1),
  score = c(5, 6, 7, 7, 8)
)
# id repeats, so this check fails and shows the error
try(isid(panel, id))
#> Error in isid(panel, id) : 
#>   Variable `id` does not uniquely identify the rows: 2 values appear more
#> than once (4 rows).
#> ℹ See them with `duplicates_list()`.

# Remove the duplicate row so id + wave uniquely identify observations
unique_panel <- dplyr::distinct(panel)
# Confirms that id + wave form a key; returns unique_panel invisibly
isid(unique_panel, id, wave)
#> Variables `id`, `wave` together uniquely identify the rows.

duplicates_report(panel, id, wave)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   copies observations surplus
#>    <int>        <int>   <int>
#> 1      1            3       0
#> 2      2            2       1

duplicates_tag(panel, id, wave)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>      id  wave score   dup
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <int>
#> 1     1     1     5     0
#> 2     1     2     6     0
#> 3     2     1     7     1
#> 4     2     1     7     1
#> 5     3     1     8     0

duplicates_list(panel, id, wave)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>      id  wave score .dup_group  .row
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>      <int> <int>
#> 1     2     1     7          1     3
#> 2     2     1     7          1     4

duplicates_drop(panel)
#> (1 row removed)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>      id  wave score
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1     1     5
#> 2     1     2     6
#> 3     2     1     7
#> 4     3     1     8
